world.title: TypeScript | Signal Harbor

paths.name: Dockhand
paths.description: Begin with everyday values, then build a small dispatch program you can understand from input to output.
paths.topics: Inference, object shapes, narrowing, functions, validation, promises, and modules

paths.name: Contract Engineer
paths.description: Make call sites carry the right data by designing types around the relationships between values.
paths.topics: Generics, key relationships, derived shapes, exhaustive states, and typed event handlers

paths.name: Boundary Operator
paths.description: Track the work that enters and leaves a system, including invalid input, asynchronous failure, and repeat delivery.
paths.topics: Runtime validation, promise handling, error results, branded identifiers, and idempotency

quests.objective: Use inference for local values and annotations for the inputs and outputs of a small function.
quests.boss_brief: Implement palletLabel. A pallet carries ten crates. Return the number of pallets needed for a nonnegative safe integer crate count. Use the exact format `Pallets: 2` for 11 crates and throw RangeError for an invalid count.
quests.side_quest: Replace the fixed capacity with a parameter. Decide which capacities are valid and test an invalid capacity before checking the result.
quests.hint2: `Math.ceil(crateCount / 10)` gives the number of pallets. Check the empty case with zero crates.
quests.debrief: A guard rejects negative, fractional, and non-finite counts. Division followed by rounding up handles exact multiples and partial pallets with one expression. Check 0, 10, and 11 crates to catch boundary errors.

quests.objective: Describe a record and let a function read a collection without granting it permission to mutate the input.
quests.boss_brief: Return the IDs of all cargo weighing at least 10 kg, in the same order as the input. Create a new array and leave the manifest alone.
quests.side_quest: Design a grouped report whose results can be read but cannot be edited through the type returned to a consumer.
quests.hint1: Try a loop that creates a fresh `string[]` before inspecting the first record.
quests.hint2: Add the ID when `weightKg >= 10`. Test a record weighing exactly 10 kg.
quests.debrief: Each selected ID is copied into a new array. The caller can add IDs to that output without changing the input array, and filtering preserves relative order.

quests.objective: Narrow a union by checking a literal tag before reading fields that belong to one case.
quests.boss_brief: Implement canUnload. An assigned arrival can unload only if its dock is open. A waiting arrival cannot unload. Use the dock list as read-only input.
quests.side_quest: Add a diverted case carrying a destination harbor. Give it a distinct message in statusText.
quests.hint1: Narrow the union using `arrival.kind` before you access `arrival.dock`.
quests.hint2: Use `openDocks.includes(arrival.dock)` inside the assigned branch, or combine both conditions with `&&`.
quests.debrief: The status test establishes which shape is present. The membership test establishes whether that dock is open. Both decisions matter, including when the assignment is to dock zero.

quests.objective: Pass a typed function as an argument and preserve meaningful falsy values when applying a default.
quests.boss_brief: Implement labelMatching. Call label once per weight that passes weight >= 0 and return the labels in input order. Negative weights and NaN fail this test.
quests.side_quest: Add a test callback that throws on its second call. Explain what the caller observes and whether the partial result ever escapes.
quests.hint1: Build a fresh array. Use the positive test `weight >= 0` to decide whether to append a label.
quests.hint2: Call `label(weight)` once per retained item. Zero is nonnegative and should reach the callback.
quests.debrief: The traversal owns the decision to include an item. The callback owns the presentation. A callback that records its inputs can show whether the traversal invokes it for the correct items and in the right order.

quests.objective: Turn untrusted JSON into a checked record by combining unknown with small runtime checks.
quests.boss_brief: Decode a dock status from raw JSON. Require a non-array record with its own nonnegative safe integer dock and boolean open. Return undefined for a syntax or shape error.
quests.side_quest: Return an error code that distinguishes invalid JSON from a missing field and a field with the wrong type.
quests.hint1: Assign `JSON.parse` to an `unknown` variable inside a try block. Handle null before checking properties.
quests.hint2: Narrow both fields with `in` and require own properties with `Object.hasOwn`. Check `open` with `typeof` so `false` is accepted.
quests.debrief: A valid object with `dock: 0` and `open: false` should pass. The strings `"0"` and `"false"` should fail. Testing those pairs proves the implementation checks types instead of relying on truthiness or coercion.

quests.objective: Await a promise, handle rejection, and keep a real value distinct from a failed request.
quests.boss_brief: Implement readGate. Await the injected status function, return open or closed on success, and return offline if the function throws or rejects.
quests.side_quest: Preserve a safe diagnostic string on the offline result without assuming every rejected value is an Error.
quests.hint1: Await the callback inside the try block so synchronous throws and rejections share the same failure branch.
quests.hint2: Map a resolved `false` to `closed`. Use `offline` only inside `catch`.
quests.debrief: A gate may be reachable and closed. Treating false as a request failure would conflate operational state with connectivity. Test resolved true, resolved false, and rejection.

quests.objective: Assemble validation and routing into a small public module with a clear interface.
quests.boss_brief: Implement a module function that routes north to dock 1 and south to dock 2 after normalizing case and whitespace. Report invalid for other values. Export the decision type and the function.
quests.side_quest: Build a separate presentation module that imports the type and formats each decision. Keep text formatting out of the routing module.
quests.hint2: Test `north`, ` SOUTH `, and a destination with no matching branch.
quests.debrief: A caller can switch on the tagged decision without parsing a message or catching an exception for an ordinary invalid destination. The standalone module can be tested with simple inputs and no infrastructure.

quests.objective: Use a generic key constraint and indexed access to preserve the relationship between a property name and its value.
quests.boss_brief: Implement a helper that gets a property from each object in a read-only list. Keep the output type linked to the selected property, so choosing a numeric field gives number[].
quests.side_quest: Accept an allowlisted field name from a text input and explain where the runtime narrowing occurs before calling pluck.
quests.hint1: The key constraint establishes that `row[key]` can be read for every row of type T.
quests.hint2: Return `rows.map(row => row[key])` and assign the result to a variable typed as the expected property array.
quests.debrief: The same code can return string[] or number[] because the return type keeps the key relationship. Test an empty list and a list of several objects with both key kinds.

quests.objective: Derive related record shapes and use satisfies to check configuration without assigning a wider type to it.
quests.boss_brief: Define a patch type derived from Dock that allows changes to capacity and open only. Apply an omitted patch field by preserving the previous value. Preserve false and zero when explicitly provided.
quests.side_quest: Add a removable note and decide how to represent preserve, replace, and clear as three different operations.
quests.hint1: `Partial<Omit<Dock, 'id'>>` expresses the same shape as the mapped type in the example.
quests.hint2: Read only the fields you intend to update. Use `??` so false and zero survive.
quests.debrief: A type-level patch narrows the API for typed callers. Reading the specific editable fields at runtime also protects the identifier if an object with extra properties reaches this function through structural compatibility.

quests.objective: Build a finite state transition and make a missing case fail TypeScript checking with never.
quests.boss_brief: Add a cancelled state with a reason. Update advance so cancelled and completed jobs are terminal, queued jobs become running, and running jobs complete. Keep the exhaustive check.
quests.side_quest: Represent a retry event and return a typed rejection if someone tries to retry a completed job.
quests.hint1: Extend the union with `{ state: 'cancelled'; id: string; reason: string }`.
quests.hint2: Return the same job object in terminal branches so the cancellation reason is retained.
quests.debrief: Each state has a clear successor. The compiler checks that every declared variant is handled, while tests can assert that terminal states keep their original data.

quests.objective: Keep a message's tag correlated with the payload expected by its handler.
quests.boss_brief: Add a delay notice with a vessel and a number of minutes. Produce `Gull delayed 5 min` for that case and keep the switch exhaustive.
quests.side_quest: Define a handler-table type from Payloads that requires one correctly typed callback for each event name.
quests.hint1: Add the event and payload in the map. The Notice union will pick up the new key automatically.
quests.hint2: Add a delay branch and read both fields from `notice.payload` after narrowing the tag.
quests.debrief: The type map is the source of the payload contract. The switch ties the runtime behavior to that contract, and its default never assignment detects a forgotten branch when a message type is added.

quests.objective: Represent the outcome of each asynchronous request while keeping the relationship to the original input order.
quests.boss_brief: Implement probeAll using an injected query. Preserve the order and name of every dock, returning a failure result for just the docks whose queries throw or reject.
quests.side_quest: Sketch how you would enforce at most four active queries. Identify where an active slot is released on failure.
quests.hint1: Use an async helper or typed async map callback so each operation catches its own failure.
quests.hint2: Pass the resulting promises to `Promise.all`. Return a Probe in both branches of the per-dock operation.
quests.debrief: A failed request no longer discards successes from other docks. A result carries its identity, and the ordered array can still be paired with the caller's inputs. Verify a mix of true, false, and a rejection.

quests.objective: Validate a string once at the boundary and give the checked identifier a distinct compile-time type.
quests.boss_brief: Make a distinct DockId brand and a parser that accepts `D-` followed by exactly two ASCII digits. The value should be usable as a string after checking.
quests.side_quest: Add a lookup that can return missing for a valid-looking dock ID. Explain why that check belongs after parsing.
quests.hint1: Start by checking `typeof value === 'string'` and then match `^D-[0-9]{2}$`.
quests.hint2: Return the branded assertion only after a successful match. Test `D-00`, `S-00`, `D-123`, and a number.
quests.debrief: The format check accepts zero digits inside an otherwise valid ID and rejects a shipment prefix. The separate marker lets functions enforce which category of checked ID they expect.

quests.objective: Connect a runtime decoder to a typed decision and a small duplicate guard with an explicit boundary.
quests.boss_brief: Implement handle with a supplied Map. A command is a non-array record with its own nonblank string id and to of 'north' or 'south'. Trim the id. Return invalid for malformed commands, route for a fresh ID, duplicate for a matching repeat, and conflict if a repeat changes the destination. Only a fresh route updates the map.
quests.side_quest: Sketch a restart-safe version. Define what is persisted, how long command IDs are retained, and what outcome a caller should see if delivery fails after dispatch recorded the ID.
quests.hint1: Narrow the input before looking it up. Extract the trimmed ID and destination only after checking both.
quests.hint2: Compare a saved destination with the incoming destination. Add the ID only on the fresh route path.
quests.debrief: Test one valid route, an identical repeat, a repeat for another destination, and an invalid object. Check the map after each call. These cases distinguish validation, conflict detection, and the one path that changes state.
